To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of the antiangiogenesis factors suramin and angiostatin can be quantified in a previously validated model for angiogenesis, using a method that is based on the three‐dimensional structure and morphology of angiogenesis.

angiostatin and/or suramin can be used in a previously validated method to quantify antiangiogenesis in an in vitro assay and that this method can be used to assess the extent of anti‐angiogenesis within the different phases of angiogenesis.

angiostatin and the antiangiogenesis agent suramin inhibit angiogenesis in an in vitro model of angiogenesis and that the effects can be quantified and related to the different phases of angiogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the quantitation of the antiangiogenic effects of angiostatin in a three‐dimensional angiogenesis model and with the elucidation of the cellular mechanisms underlying the angiostatic action of angiostatin.
the identification and characterisation of angiostatic factors, and with the development of a new in vitro model for the quantitation of angiogenic processes and their modulation.
the development of a new in vitro model for the quantitation of the angiogenic process and its application in angiostatic therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
angiostatin and, to a lesser extent, suramin, are potent angiostatic substances, which may be useful for treatment of tumours.
antiangiogenic effects of angiostatin are quantifiable and can be differentiated from those of suramin, and that antiangiogenesis can be studied in the various phases of angiogenesis.
angiogenesis is a complex and dynamic process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
angiostatin and/or suramin could be used as antiangiogenesis drugs for the treatment of tumour angiogenesis.
angiostatin and its effects are dose‐dependent, and that suramin can be used as a potential inhibitor for angiogenesis.
angiogenesis is a complex and dynamic process, which can be inhibited at different stages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
angiostatin and the related angiostatic factor suramin have different modes of antiangiogenesis.
the effects of angiostatic factors can be quantitatively assessed and that the method can be used in the development of new antiangiogenic therapies.
angiostatin and/or suramin may be useful in antiangiogenic therapy, and that the in vitro model we have developed can be used to quantify the antiangiogenic effect of angiostatin or suramin.
